subject: Design inquiry: blind-signing HSM connector for on-prem Redwood Private
messages:
From: ops-security@finbank.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: coresec-labs@example.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Design inquiry: blind-signing HSM connector for on-prem Redwood Private

Hi Aditya,

We're evaluating Redwood Private for a use-case that requires an HSM-backed blind-signing flow: FinBank wants to issue short-lived, signed inference tokens for internal customers, where the HSM should never expose raw signing keys to operator or host OS. High-level asks:

- Confirm Redwood supports BYOK imports into customer HSMs (we plan to import a root signing key).
- We need a blind-sign flow (Redwood signs blinded token payloads and returns signatures) such that the HSM never releases the unblinded private key material.
- Operator separation: how do you prevent NOC/operator access to signing operations or key material?
- Auditing: required cryptographic audit trail per signing operation (timestamp, signing key id, caller identity, nonce).
- Rotation / compromise recovery: what rotation primitives do you recommend? Can we do split-escrow for root keys?
- Network: HSM will live in our on-prem DMZ with a restricted management VLAN. We can open mutual TLS to a Redwood KMS proxy at customer VPC.

Attached is a short set of questions from our external security reviewer (CoreSec Labs) — they prefer an explicit dataflow diagram and a list of required HSM features (FIPS, remote attestation).

Can you outline an architecture and runbook options? We have an upcoming compliance window in Q1 and need a recommended design and checklist.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
FinBank SecOps
ops-security@finbank.com

Attachment: finbank-question-set.pdf (application/pdf)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: ops-security@finbank.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, coresec-labs@example.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Design inquiry: blind-signing HSM connector for on-prem Redwood Private

Maya — thanks for the clear ask. High level response and a proposed architecture below; I attached a preliminary diagram and an HSM interface spec for review.

Summary (short): Redwood Private can be configured to operate with customer-managed HSMs (BYOK) and run a KMS-proxy inside the customer VPC. For a blind-signing flow we recommend an HSM-resident root signing key (never exported) combined with per-session ephemeral wrapping keys and an HMAC-based attestation envelope. Operator/admin accounts do not get access to plaintext key material; all operations are mediated by the HSM and recorded in the audit log.

Proposed architecture (high level):
- Customer HSM (on-prem, e.g., Thales nShield or Luna) holds a non-exportable root signing key (K_root).
- Customer deploys Redwood KMS-proxy (container) in their VPC / management VLAN that speaks mTLS to Redwood control plane for telemetry only. All signing RPCs travel from Redwood Private runtime nodes to the KMS-proxy over an internal private link (mutual TLS + client certs).
- Blind-signing protocol: client -> Redwood runtime submits blinded payload; runtime forwards blinded payload to KMS-proxy; KMS-proxy forwards to HSM using vendor API. HSM returns blind signature. Runtime returns signature to caller. At no point is K_root material exposed outside HSM.
- Ephemeral wrapping keys: for additional separation we recommend generating short-lived ephemeral signing keys inside the HSM derived from K_root via an HKDF-based derivation inside the HSM (so derivation occurs in-protected boundary). Ephemeral keys have limited TTL (minutes-hours) and are referenced by key IDs in audit logs.
- Attestation and integrity: use HSM-supplied attestation (certified per op) or TPM-based host attestation for the KMS-proxy host; signatures of the attestation should be logged and surfaced to customer SIEM.
- Auditing: every HSM operation logs (timestamp, operation id, key id, requester cert thumbprint, request nonce). Redwood will forward these logs to the customer SIEM via a secure syslog endpoint or S3 bucket.

Operational controls / separation:
- Operator roles: split NOC/crypto-operational roles. NOC monitors health/metrics; crypto ops approve key ceremonies and rotation.
- No console access to HSM private key: Redwood engineers will not be able to export K_root or derived keys. Access to HSM management interface can be restricted to customer admin ACLs.
- Emergency access: documented key-ceremony for split-escrow; Redwood supports integrating a multi-party unseal (threshold scheme) if required.

Rotation/recovery recommendations:
- Root key (K_root) should be rotated only via an in-person or multi-party import/ceremony; frequency: quarterly or per-customer policy.
- Use ephemeral derived keys for daily traffic; rotate ephemeral keys frequently (e.g., every 6–12 hours) to limit exposure window.
- Maintain a signed key-version manifest in the customer's S3 (or on-prem artifact store) with hashes and provenance.

Questions for you (so we can finalize the runbook):
1) Which exact HSM vendor/model are you standardizing on (we have minor vendor-specific API variants)?
2) Is in-person key import/ceremony possible for K_root?
3) Regulatory constraints (FIPS/TAA) we should be aware of?
4) Do you have a central SIEM endpoint we should push audit logs to?

Next steps: if this direction looks good we'll prepare an ops runbook and an on-site/instrumentation checklist.

Thanks — tagging Mina for ops/runbook details and Markus for vendor-specific notes.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Design inquiry: blind-signing HSM connector for on-prem Redwood Private

Thanks Aditya — a few practical ops notes to include in the runbook:

- Fallback policy: define a pre-approved fallback (alternate key id on a dedicated HSM cluster) and an automatic traffic drain to a non-signing safe-mode if the HSM is unavailable to avoid silent failures.
- Health probes should be read-only and not count against signing quotas; rate-limit signing RPCs to prevent accidental DoS.
- Incident playbook: compromise detection (e.g., anomalous signing volume, signature shape changes) -> immediate revoke of ephemeral keys -> initiate key-ceremony for K_root audit.
- Backup/escrow: recommend split-escrow using at least 3 parties (customer security, Redwood trust ops, third-party custodian) with thresholds defined.

I also want to call out an implementation constraint: some HSMs do not support blind-signing primitives natively; we may need to implement blinding/unblinding in the KMS-proxy with the HSM providing raw sign operation only under attested conditions. That increases the attack surface for the KMS-proxy and will require hardened host attestation (TPM/SEV) and a minimized TCB.

I'll draft a runbook section covering: pre-reqs, network ports, mTLS cert cadence, key ceremony checklist, emergency rotation steps, and a daily ops checklist.

Mina Haddad
Director, Platform Reliability

Aditya / Mina,

Thanks — helpful. Answers to your questions below:

1) HSM vendor/model: Thales nShield 8000 (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified).
2) Key import ceremony: yes, our infra team can support in-person import with an operator present. We prefer split-escrow retention (3-party).
3) Regulatory constraints: must maintain FIPS validated crypto and provide evidence for SOC2 Type II. TAA applies to any cloud components; on-prem HSM is allowed.
4) SIEM: Splunk with secure-forwarder endpoint (hosted in our audit VLAN). We'll provide creds and URL during onboarding.

Additional constraints: we require that any KMS-proxy code that handles blinded material run on customer-managed hosts with attestation; hosting in Redwood-managed infrastructure is not acceptable for this connector.

One more ask: can you document entropy sources and RNG verification steps used during key derivation and ephemeral key generation? CoreSec flagged this as high priority.

Regards,
Maya Patel
FinBank SecOps
ops-security@finbank.com

- Vendor-specific call with Markus (Thales experience) to confirm API mapping and blind-sign support — propose Wed 2026-11-25 10:00 PT.

Action items (FinBank):
- Confirm availability for on-site key import ceremony (preferred week of 2026-12-13).
- Provide Splunk forwarder endpoint and cert thumbprint for testing ingestion.

Notes on entropy/RNG:
- We'll document required HSM RNG checks: vendor-supplied DRBG health checks, NIST SP 800-90B/90A checks, and optional external entropy injection procedures. For ephemeral key derivation, we recommend (and will document) HKDF with per-session nonce + HSM-resident salt; all derivation happens inside the HSM when supported.

Do you want us to produce a short joint runbook draft (Redwood + FinBank sections) or separate vendor-neutral runbook first? I recommend a single joint runbook for the compliance audit.

I'll schedule the vendor call and loop in procurement for the MSA/PO. Sending a DocuSign packet for the connector NDA now: https://app.docusign.com/packets/5f2b9-connector-nda
